hero.title: Everything KeeperHub does. <accent>Just ask.</accent>
hero.subtitle: KeeperHub automates anything onchain. This is how you use it — say what you want in your own words, and the copilot finds the right action, fills it in and runs it.
hero.enterHint: press enter to open in the app

heading.title: You don't learn KeeperHub. <accent>You talk to it.</accent>
heading.subtitle: 442 actions, 34 integrations, 24 networks. You never have to know which one you need — say what you want and the copilot picks it.

price.title: What's ETH worth right now?
price.description: Live Chainlink feeds, read straight off the chain, with the last twelve updates drawn beside the number.

holdings.title: What am I holding?
holdings.description: Your organisation's wallet across every network it touches, with the empty ones dimmed rather than hidden.

send.title: Send 10 USDC to alice.eth
send.description: It fills in the amount, the recipient, the network and the token, shows you, and waits for your click.

supply.title: Supply 50 USDC to Aave
supply.description: Lending, staking, swaps, bridges. It checks the position first and tells you if it would not work.

automate.title: Watch gas and tell me at 20 gwei
automate.description: Describe it once and it becomes a real KeeperHub automation, saved switched off until you turn it on.

explain.title: What can you actually do?
explain.description: Ask and it searches its own registry — every action KeeperHub ships, with what each one touches.

heading.title: Not a wall of text. <accent>A card.</accent>
heading.subtitle: Every answer arrives as something you can read at a glance and act on. Drag the stack.

price.title: A price, and where it came from
price.description: The figure, the feed, the network and the time it was published.

write.title: Every field, filled in and editable
write.description: Change the amount or the recipient and it checks the whole thing again.

dryRun.title: KeeperHub tries it first
dryRun.description: If it would not succeed, you are told why before anything is signed.

receipt.title: A receipt read back off the chain
receipt.description: Block, hash and status — not a tool saying it went fine.

automation.title: A workflow you can read
automation.description: The trigger, every step in order, and a switch that starts it.

heading.title: Describe it once. <accent>It keeps running.</accent>
heading.subtitle: The copilot builds every kind of start KeeperHub has, out of a sentence. It saves switched off, shows you what it would do, and waits for you to turn it on.

manual.title: On demand
manual.body: Runs when you say so, and only then.

schedule.title: On a schedule
schedule.body: Every hour, every morning, the first of the month.

block.title: Every N blocks
block.body: Counted on the chain itself, not on a clock.

event.title: On a contract event
event.body: A log fires, your steps run.

webhook.title: On a webhook
webhook.body: Anything that can make a request can start it.

payment.title: On a payment
payment.body: Money lands, the workflow picks it up.

automations.footnote: List them, change them, run one now or delete it — all from the chat.

heading.title: A sentence goes in. <accent>A receipt comes out.</accent>
heading.subtitle: Four steps. Questions answer straight away; anything that moves value stops and asks.

ask.title: You say what you want
ask.body: No SDK, no contract address, no calldata. Type it the way you would say it to a person.

resolve.title: It finds the action
resolve.body: 442 of them across 34 integrations, generated from KeeperHub's own registry. It picks the one you meant and works out what it still needs to know.

confirm.title: It shows you before it runs
confirm.body: Anything that moves value stops as a card with every field filled in and editable. KeeperHub tries it first and tells you if it would fail.

receipt.title: You get proof it happened
receipt.body: The transaction read back off the chain, kept as a record of its own — so deleting the conversation never deletes the evidence.

heading.title: One key into <accent>your</accent> KeeperHub.
heading.subtitle: The copilot signs in with KeeperHub, so it only needs its own settings. A kh_ key with mcp:write scope connects any other MCP client you already run.

finalCta.title: Everything KeeperHub does. <accent>Just ask.</accent>
finalCta.body: Ask a question and the answer comes straight back. Ask it to do something and it shows you exactly what that is, then waits for your click.
